newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds slide lower with Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds slide lower with Treasuries.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities turned sharply lower on Thursday, but yield spreads over Treasuries narrowed.
Heightened fears of an interest-rate hike at the March 25 Federal Reserve policy meeting drove the faster decline in Treasuries, analysts said.
Declines in mortgages were less-pronounced, as pass-throughs took their cues from Treasuries, mortgage traders said.
"There's been buying of premium paper, as usually happens in these situations," one trader said.
In a bear market, prices of shorter-duration mortgages tend to be more stable than the longer-duration, lower-coupon issues, according to analysts.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was off 13/32 at 99-12/32, yielding 101 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae issues were off 14/32 at 99-12/32 and Freddie Mac paper was off 13/32 at 99-19/32.
The 10-year Treasury note was off 22/32 at 6.71 percent.
Talk of a Fed tightening resurfaced in the wake of a strong revision to January retail sales.
